get.description: Returns the project name, the number of Missions the service lists, the recorded Spec Kitty and schema versions, the health badge, the current branch and the latest Mission activity. The read is side-effect-free and runs no drift scan; its cost grows with the Mission count (see the Project schema). A Mission whose declared coordination branch no longer exists, or whose remote cannot be reached, is read from its own directory and the answer is still a 200; any other resolver error is a 500 Problem, as for GET /drift.

schema.title: Project
schema.description: The project the service reports on: its name, the number of Missions it lists (missionCount), and five properties of the project's state: specKittyVersion and schemaVersion (what the project recorded), health (whether that schema is one the serving build supports), currentBranch (the branch checked out) and lastActivityAt (the latest Mission activity). It never carries a path, a worktree location or a credential. GET /project is read-only, side-effect-free and safe to call once per recent project; it runs no drift scan, and health never depends on a drift finding. It is not free: missionCount and lastActivityAt need every listed Mission, so the read resolves each Mission's read directory through git queries, which can include network probes for a Mission whose declared coordination branch is absent locally, and reduces its event log. The cost grows with the Mission count and, for those Missions, with the network, so side-effect-free does not mean not network-free.

name.description: The project slug, the short human-readable name of the repository the service reports on.

specKittyVersion.description: The Spec Kitty version the project recorded in .kittify/metadata.yaml (spec_kitty.version). Null when the file is absent, empty, unreadable or not the expected shape, when it records no version, and when the recorded value is not a string of the pattern; the product's own placeholder for a missing version never leaves the service. A strict field: projected or null, never redacted.

schemaVersion.description: The schema version the project recorded (spec_kitty.schema_version), exactly as the command line coerces it: a numeric string, a float and a boolean in the file are served as the integer the CLI's coercion gives (the string "3" is 3, 3.9 is 3, true is 1). Null when the file is absent or unreadable, the field is absent, or the value is not an integer after that coercion.

health.description: healthy exactly when schemaVersion is not null and lies in the range of schema versions the serving build supports; otherwise schema_drift. The range is that of the serving build, so the same project reads healthy or schema_drift depending on which build serves it. It rolls up the three non-compatible schema statuses (unmigrated, outdated, cli_outdated); the finer split stays in schemaVersion. It never depends on a drift finding. This property is provisional, and a client must tolerate a health value it does not know.

x-derived.rule: healthy when schemaVersion is not null and MIN_SUPPORTED_SCHEMA <= schemaVersion <= MAX_SUPPORTED_SCHEMA of the serving build; otherwise schema_drift.

currentBranch.description: The branch the project's HEAD names, read from the HEAD file with no process started; an unborn branch is its name. Null means no branch name this contract can carry: a detached HEAD, no repository, an unreadable or unparseable HEAD, a name that fails the pattern or is too long, or a name that is a host path. It does not separate those cases. A served name is user-authored text served as stored, so it can carry a handle, as Workspace.laneBranch can.

lastActivityAt.description: The latest MissionHead.lastActivityAt over exactly the Missions GET /missions lists, compared as instants (different offsets are ordered by instant, not by text) and served as that Mission's own string. Null when no Mission is listed and when every listed Mission has null activity. A Mission whose status.json cannot be read leaves its activity out (null if that was the only source); an event log that cannot be decoded or parsed fails the whole read with a 500.

x-derived.rule: The latest instant of lastActivityAt over the Missions GET /missions lists; null when none is listed or none has activity; a Mission with an unreadable status.json adds no activity, and an event log that cannot be decoded or parsed fails the read (500).

get.description: Returns one page of Mission overviews. The order is a total key: createdAt descending, with ties broken by missionId ascending. Paging uses the shared opaque page cursor: pass the nextPageCursor of one response as pageCursor to fetch the next page, and stop when hasNextPage is false. A pageCursor that is malformed, forged or no longer valid is answered with 400 and a problem whose code is invalid_page_cursor.

phases.description: Exactly five entries, in the order specify, plan, tasks, implement, review. No existing reader computes these, so the rules are owned by this contract. Specify, plan and tasks are evaluated alike: complete with basis artifact when the planning file (spec.md, plan.md or tasks.md respectively) exists in the Mission directory; else complete with basis lifecycle_event when the matching Completed lifecycle event (SpecifyCompleted, PlanCompleted or TasksCompleted) exists; else in_progress with basis lifecycle_event when the matching Started event exists; else pending with basis artifact. Implement and review always carry basis derived_from_status_lanes and use statusLaneCounts and wpTotal, evaluated in this order. Implement: complete when wpTotal is above 0 and every work package is for_review, in_review, approved, done or canceled; else pending when no work package has left planned or blocked (a Mission with no work packages is pending); else in_progress. Review: complete when wpTotal is above 0 and every work package is done or canceled; else pending when no work package is for_review, in_review, approved or done; else in_progress. There is no lifecycle event for implement or review. The Mission phase is not the glossary phase.

items.title: MissionPhase
items.description: One of the five phases of a Mission's workflow: specify, plan, tasks, implement, review. This is the Mission phase, a stage of the workflow. It is not the glossary term phase and it is not the phaseLabel of a work package. Each entry says how far the phase has got and what that statement rests on. The first three phases rest on a planning artifact or a lifecycle event; implement and review rest on the status lanes of the work packages and never on an artifact.

name.description: Which phase this entry describes. The five phases always appear in this order.

status.description: How far the phase has got. The rule for each phase is written on the phases field of MissionDetail.

basis.description: What the status rests on. artifact: a planning file exists, or no evidence exists and the phase is pending. lifecycle_event: a Started or Completed lifecycle event. derived_from_status_lanes: the status lane counts, used for implement and review only.

For specify, plan and tasks: the planning file exists, then complete by artifact; else the Completed lifecycle event, then complete by lifecycle_event; else the Started event, then in_progress by lifecycle_event; else pending by artifact. For implement: complete when wpTotal is above 0 and every work package is for_review, in_review, approved, done or canceled; else pending when none has left planned or blocked; else in_progress. For review: complete when wpTotal is above 0 and every work package is done or canceled; else pending when none is for_review, in_review, approved or done; else in_progress. Implement is evaluated before review.

get.summary: Stream the changes of Missions as server-sent events.
get.description:
A change stream, served as text/event-stream. OpenAPI 3.1 has no native way to describe a
stream of named events, so the stream is documented here as a convention; the schema of the
200 response is the schema of the data field of each event, not of the whole body.

Event names and data schemas. There are exactly three event names, each with one data
schema, and no other event name is ever sent:

- `status-transition` -> StatusTransitionEvent: a work package changed status lane.
- `mission-lifecycle` -> MissionLifecycleEvent: the Mission was created, or a planning phase started or completed.
- `log-truncated` -> LogTruncatedEvent: the Mission's event log shrank or changed; resynchronise.

Framing. Each event is sent as an `event:` line with the event name, an `id:` line with the
StreamCursorString of the event, a `data:` line with the JSON of the data schema, and a blank
line. The id is the same string the streamCursor parameter and the Last-Event-ID header
accept. Two kinds of event carry no `id:` line, so that a browser's automatic Last-Event-ID
never holds a position that cannot be resumed from. Every event of an unscoped stream (no
missionId) is sent without an `id:` line, because a cursor is a position in one Mission's log
and the unscoped stream interleaves Missions. A log-truncated event is sent without an `id:`
line on every stream, because its own cursor is the reset position, offset 0, and resuming
from it would replay the whole log; the cursor stays inside its data. A heartbeat is a comment
line, `: heartbeat`, sent every 30 seconds; it carries no data and is not an event.

Projection. Raw rows of the Mission's event log never appear. Only a status transition and
seven lifecycle types (MissionCreated, SpecifyStarted, SpecifyCompleted, PlanStarted,
PlanCompleted, TasksStarted, TasksCompleted) are forwarded; annotation rows, decision-point
rows, retrospective rows, reviewer self-approval rows, work package creation rows and every
unknown row are dropped, never forwarded. The seven lifecycle types are owned by this
contract and are a subset of the runtime's twelve; a type added upstream later is dropped.

Scope and ordering. With missionId the stream carries that Mission only; a missionId that
names no Mission is answered with 404 before any event is sent. Without it the
stream carries every Mission, live only: it never replays and no cursor can be used. A new
connection without a cursor is live only from the moment it connects. Order is guaranteed
per Mission, in the order of that Mission's log; there is no order across Missions, and a
log-truncated event of one Mission may arrive between events of others.

Resume. A cursor is a StreamCursor position in one Mission's own physical event log (the
TailCursor of the tail reader, the same position `spec-kitty events tail` resumes from), so
it is valid for that log only and always needs missionId. Send the id of the last event you
consumed as streamCursor, or let the browser send it as Last-Event-ID. A cursor that cannot
be trusted is refused before any event is sent, with a problem whose code is negative,
out_of_range, misaligned or content_mismatch (the reasons of the tail reader's
ResumeRefused), or cursor_without_mission when a cursor comes without missionId. The status
of each code is fixed: negative, misaligned and cursor_without_mission are 400; out_of_range
and content_mismatch are 409 (StreamRefusal states this as a checkable rule). A browser
EventSource cannot read the body of a refused connection, it only closes, so a consumer that
must tell these refusals apart opens the stream with a fetch that streams the response body
instead of EventSource. After a log-truncated event on a Mission-scoped stream the last id the
browser holds is the one before the truncation, and a reconnect with it is refused; the consumer
then resynchronises as below.

Consumer actions. On log-truncated, discard the stored cursor of that Mission, read the
Mission detail again, and resume from the streamCursor of that detail; the cursor inside the
event is only the reset one, offset 0 with the digest of the empty input. A value inside a
known kind that a consumer does not know, such as an unlisted eventType, is treated as
unknown and is not a failure; the schemas stay closed, so a producer must not send one.

Provisional. These parts are provisional: the framing of the stream and which events carry an id line, the text form of the cursor, the rule that
streamCursor wins over Last-Event-ID, the HTTP status of each refusal and the heartbeat
interval are conventions owned by this contract; the tail reader has no text form of a
cursor and no transport. They are open on #5528 and may change before release. No emitter,
server or transport exists yet: this describes a stream that a later change implements.

x-provisional.open_decision: The framing of the stream (the event:, id: and data: lines and the blank line), which events carry an id: line (none on an unscoped stream, none for log-truncated), the heartbeat comment line and its interval of 30 seconds, and the HTTP status of each refusal (400 or 409) are conventions owned by this contract: the tail reader has no transport. They are proposals open on #5528 and may change before release.

parameters.name: streamCursor
parameters.description: Resumes the stream of one Mission after the event that carried this cursor, in the text form offset, colon, invariant. schema.title: StreamCursorString
schema.description: The text form of a StreamCursor: the decimal byte offset, a colon, and the 64 lowercase hexadecimal characters of the invariant, for example an offset of 0 followed by a colon and the digest of the empty input. It is the value of the streamCursor query parameter, of the Last-Event-ID request header and of the SSE id field of the events of a Mission-scoped stream (log-truncated carries no id), all the same string. The offset has no leading zeros, so one cursor has exactly one text. The JSON object form, StreamCursor, is what travels inside the data of an event. It has no relationship to the opaque page cursor used for paging lists.

That streamCursor wins over the Last-Event-ID header when both are sent is a proposal for the event stream convention, open on #5528.

get.summary: Read where derived state disagrees with its source.
get.description: Scans the Missions of the project, or the one named by missionId, and reports each place where a derived file disagrees with the record that decides it. Three kinds are reported: the status snapshot disagrees with the status event log, one of the two status files is missing, and an expected lane branch, or the Mission branch (the coordination branch that meta.json names, else the Mission branch of the lane manifest), has no local branch. A scan reads and never repairs; Rescan is a second call, and scannedAt is the time of this scan. Findings are sorted and at most 1000, with truncated true only when MORE than 1000 existed (exactly 1000 is false), and findings: [] means the scan ran and found none. A Mission whose declared coordination branch no longer exists is scanned from its own directory, which can lag the coordination surface. The stock coordination resolver may query remotes, so the outcome depends on the network. An unreachable remote leaves the Mission read from its own directory, and the answer is still a 200; a reachable remote that lacks the declared branch is likewise read from its own directory; any other resolver error is a 500 drift_scan_unreadable. The scan is refused as a whole, never partly answered: a missionId that names no Mission is a 404, and a Mission the scan cannot read is a 500.

get.summary: List the Op invocation records of the project.
get.description: Returns one page of the Op invocations of the project, newest first: startedAt descending, with ties broken by invocationId descending. An Op is one governed invocation of an agent profile on an action, recorded in the Ops directory. Paging uses the shared opaque page cursor: pass the nextPageCursor of one response as pageCursor to fetch the next page, and stop when hasNextPage is false. A pageCursor that is malformed, forged, or issued for another profile is answered with 400 and a problem whose code is invalid_page_cursor. The optional profile query parameter keeps the Ops of one profile; a profile that matches no Op gives an empty page, and a profile that fails its pattern is a 400 problem. Records with legacy or malformed content are skipped, never served and never a failure: a record of an older shape, an empty or truncated file, a file whose name differs from its invocation id, an index entry that names no file and a malformed field are skipped and counted in skippedCount, over the same candidate set as totalCount and independent of profile, because a skipped record has no reliable profile. totalCount is the number of served Ops matching profile, and it can lag the newest records, which an Op appended after the read began may not yet be part of. An Op is closed when its own file holds a completion or the closure spine holds a record for its id. A directory, the closure spine or an Op file that exists but cannot be opened is a 500 problem, never an empty page. The operation never starts an agent and never writes.

Skipped records are in neither items nor totalCount. A project with no Ops directory answers an empty page with both counts 0.

items.description: One Op: a governed invocation of an agent profile on an action, as recorded in the Ops directory, with the state of its closure. It is open until its own file holds a completion or the closure spine holds a record for its id, and then closed; an open Op has no outcome, closer, completion instant or evidence. A record of an older shape or an unreadable record is never served as an Op; it is skipped and counted. Record fields left out on purpose, because they are free text, model identity or internal routing state: request_text, model_id, governance_context_hash, governance_context_available and router_confidence. The schema is closed, so a payload carrying any of them is invalid.
